**What you should be able to do after this meeting.** Design a study in writing under exam conditions. Then say which AI modality suits which job, interrogate a real dataset through one, and catch something wrong with it.

## Before class

**Reading.** Review

No quiz this meeting.

## Session A · 2:05–3:15

**Midterm.** You are given a situation and asked to design a study to evaluate it, in writing. The question. The design. What data it requires. And what would undermine it.

## Session B · 3:35–4:30

Every session B opens with a ten-minute team check-in: what you did
since last week, what is stuck, and who is doing what next. Written
down, and handed in with that session's work.

First, the modalities. 'Use AI' is four different things, and they fail differently. Chat answers from memory, and will invent a citation. File upload with code execution writes and runs real code on your data, so the output is checkable. Retrieval answers from documents you supplied. Agents act over several steps, and compound a mistake made early. The one you want here is the second. Knowing why is the point. Then real data in front of you, and the meeting-9 checklist put to work: summaries, joins, quick plots. Then the harder half. Knowing whether the answer is right without reading the code. Row counts across a join. Totals against a published figure. Five raw records read by hand. And what not to upload, and why.

Your team's output is submitted before you leave.

## Due

Data feasibility memo — full, end of week
